full_judgment:
KM Hafizul Alam, J: This Rule, at the instance of the petitioner, was issued under section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the impugned order No. 8 dated 28-11-2013 passed by the learned Divisional Special Judge, Sylhet in Special Case No. 22 of 2013 corresponding to GR Case No. 79 of 2006 arising out of Chatok Police Station Case No. 17 dated 30-4-2006 under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, discharging the accused-opposite-party Nos. 2-5 upon allowing the application filed by the opposite-party under section 241(A) of the Code of Criminal Procedure should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts, relevant for the purpose of the disposal of the Rule, in short, are that one Md Shafiqur Rahman Bhuiyan, District Durnity Damon Officer, Cumilla on 30-4-2006 as informant lodged a First Information Report (in short FIR) against the accused-opposite-parties Nos.2-5. The allegations, inter alit?, were that the former Chairman of Chatok Pourashova Abdul Wahed Monju alias Monju Mia, Designer Moniruddin Ahmed, Accountant Santosh Kumar Das and Contractor Syed Rezaul Haque in connivance with each other by violating the Bidhimala and violating the terms and conditions of tender process and by not following the approved design constructed the Pouro Building and caused damage Taka 52,43,953 from the public fund. In the primary approval letter of the Ministry of Local Government there was condition that before constructing the building sample of soil had to be tested and soil test report was required to be sent to the Ministry for final foundation design. Accordingly the soil test report was sent to the Chief Engineer, LGED for approval of the final foundation designed on 19-6-2003. In the meantime the Chairman by completing the tender process through tender committee sent the same to the Ministry for approval. In this way the accused Chairman Monju Mia in connivance with each other by misusing his power caused loss of Taka 52, 43,953 to the government. In order to suppress the measurement the work and quality they also destroyed the related measurement of book. At the time of inquiry the independent engineer declared that the newly building as "ঝুঁকিপূর্ণ". By this way the opposite party No. 2-5 have also been benefited. 

 5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned order of discharge dated 28-11-2013 passed by the learned Divisional Special Judge, Sylhet in Special Case No. 22 of 2013, the informant as petitioner approached this court with an application under section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and obtained this Rule on 1-4-2019. 

 9. He points out that pursuant to the soil test the final design was required to be approved by the concern ministry and after approval of the foundation design the building was to be constructed but in the instant case the opposite party No.2-5 in connivance with each other without getting the sold test report and without getting any approval of the concern authority constructed the building and thereby caused damaged Taka 52,43,953 of the Government money and, as such, the Rule may be discharged. 

 10. He submits that there is specific allegation against the accused-opposite-party Nos.2-5 and as per section 10 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, the government has no authority to withdraw the case filed by the Anti-Corruption Commission as such the impugned order of discharge is liable to be set-aside. 

 17. We have perused the application under section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, counter affidavit and other prosecution materials annexed thereto. 

 20. From the above prosecution materials it appears that there is specific allegation against the accused-opposite party No.2-5 who in collusion with others caused damage of Taka 52, 43,953 to the Government. 

 27. In view of the above discussion and principles laid down by our apex court, we are of the view that there is no scope to discharge the accused at the time of charge hearing accepting the prosecution version when prima-facie case is disclosed in the prosecution materials. The disputed question of facts, the defense version of the accused, defense materials and prima-facie case only be proved/ disproved/ discarded at the time of trial by taking evidences. Apart from this there is also an important question of law is involved with the case as to whether the Government can withdraw the case filed by the Anti-corruption Commission. In this regard the section 10(4) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 is reproduced as below- 

 28. From the above provision it is very much apparent that the Government cannot withdraw the case filed by the Anti-Corruption Commission.
